title: Choose the visual world for brickbot.ro (bolder hand)
question: A bolder hand with the students at the centre. The first card leads by deal order. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Kit Quilt
options.lineage: a memory quilt pieced from ten seasons of team shirts
options.thesis: BrickBot as a quilt pieced from the team's own shirts: every block is a season, a photo of the students in it, and a hand-written label.
options.viewport: The first screen is a quilt of unequal blocks. The big centre block is the Nationals celebration; smaller blocks hold students at the robot, the drive team and a school visit. The headline is set on a burgundy patch, and the Support action is a yellow patch stitched into the grid.
options.risk: Can feel soft and crafty for an electric brand. The yellow stitch has to carry the energy, running like current.

raised.raise: Yellow rationed like a lit digit: the running stitch is the only glowing thing, so it reads as current.
Each section is one compositional problem solved on one block grid: no generic card rows.
Every block is a link with a visible trail to its season, so the quilt doubles as navigation.

options.label: Hand-Processed Reel
options.thesis: The team's seasons as a reel of film: students in every frame, edge-coded with event and year, with yellow light leaks for the electric charge.
options.viewport: A giant film frame of the Nationals celebration fills the screen inside sprocket margins. The edge code reads 15996 · FOCȘANI · 2016→. A yellow leak blooms over the headline, and Support is stamped as an edge-code button.
options.case: Puts students first and cinematically. It loses narrowly on clarity: the film language can feel like a documentary rather than a team asking for support.
options.risk: A grain filter applied everywhere becomes an Instagram preset.

options.label: Season Rental Wall
options.thesis: Ten seasons as clamshell tapes on a lit shelf: the covers are team photos, the spines read the season names, and hand-written shelf talkers do the persuading.
options.viewport: A shelf of season spines across the screen, with the current season pulled face-out showing the team photo. A marker talker says why to back them; the Support tag hangs on the shelf.
options.case: Memorable and fun for strangers, with students on every cover. It loses on clarity: it's a better seasons archive than a home page for a sponsor.
options.risk: Retro novelty, and the burgundy has to fight the fluorescent blue.

options.label: HyperCard Shoebox
options.thesis: The team as a stack of linked cards.
options.viewport: A black-and-white card with painted buttons.
options.case: No colour at all: it erases the brand yellow and greys out the students' photos.
options.kept: Visible link trails: every block is a door.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.case: Numbers instead of people, and the impact numbers don't exist yet.

options.label: Bauhaus Workshop
options.viewport: Geometric shapes on a white table.
options.case: The white ground breaks dark-first, and abstraction hides the students.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark robotics-team site done well: big photo hero, stats row, latest season, sponsor strip.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed photo, a headline with two buttons, and a stats row under it.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other FTC team site, which is the problem the brief named.
